title: Additive indecomposability of the primes
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: The proof, after OpenAI's 2026 paper, of Ostmann's conjecture (the inverse Goldbach problem): if A and B are sets of nonnegative integers with at least two elements each, then A + B differs from the set of primes in infinitely many places. A sieve for finitely many shifts reduces to two infinite summands; Elsholtz's square-root bounds and collision stability; decorrelation of the residue supports from translated quadratic characters (an amplified moment, Bonami's inequality, Weyl sums, a common rational centre, Heath-Brown's quadratic large sieve, the zero-free region with Page's and Siegel's theorems) and from characters of higher order (Kneser's addition theorem, Cauchy-Schwarz transfers, anchor codes); a supply of nonsparse Fourier transforms from coverage of every large prime; a finite-field comparison of binary trees of rational maps; a positive statistic, its transfers, and the arithmetic comparison estimates that contradict it.
prerequisites: the large sieve inequality and Montgomery's arithmetic large sieve (course Dirichlet L-functions and primes in progressions, NT-DIRL-12)
Dirichlet characters, real primitive characters as Kronecker symbols, Gauss sums (NT-DIRL-01, NT-DIRL-03)

the functional equation, zero-free regions with Landau-Page, zero counting and explicit formulas, Siegel's theorem, log-free zero density for the family of primitive characters (NT-DIRL-05, NT-DIRL-07, NT-DIRL-08, NT-DIRL-10, NT-DIRL-17)
Mertens' estimates, the prime number theorem with the classical error term, Poisson summation (course The Riemann zeta function, NT-ZETA-02, NT-ZETA-04, NT-ZETA-09, NT-ZETA-12)
quadratic reciprocity (course Algebraic number theory, lesson Cyclotomic fields)
finite Fourier analysis on Z/qZ and on its unit group
